title: QuickAir
description: Nigeria's B2B flight aggregation platform for travel agencies. Real-time concurrent search across 12 airline portals, automated ticket issuance, and a pay-as-you-go wallet.
features: 3-tier concurrent scraper architecture: Wakanow aggregator API, headless-browser scrapers (go-rod/Chrome), and lightweight HTTP scrapers running as a fan-out across 12 Nigerian airlines
Real-time incremental flight results streamed to the client via Server-Sent Events (SSE) as each scraper finishes
Browser semaphore singleton limiting concurrent Chrome instances based on available server RAM, with a separate semaphore for the ticket-issuance worker pool
Shared Crane.aero and vars portal automation library reused across multiple sister airlines — a single DOM-interaction codebase for all Crane and vars backed carriers
Wakanow fallback signal: direct scrapers yield their results to the aggregator and only run independently if Wakanow fails or times out
Chrome profile pool per airline — credential slots managed as a buffered-channel token bucket, with stealth flags to suppress browser automation fingerprints
Durable ticket issuance queue: jobs written to Postgres first, claimed atomically by workers, with dependent-segment ordering (return flight waits for outbound PNR) and admin force-cancel
5-step persistent job poller running every 5 minutes to recover orphaned, stale, and exhausted queue records across restarts
HMAC-SHA256 partner API with replay-attack protection (5-minute timestamp window) for external system integrations
Pay-as-you-go wallet via Paystack with dedicated virtual accounts — agencies fund exactly what they need, no minimum balance
Granular per-staff permission flags (search, issue, view bookings, view balance) enforced at middleware level
Admin scraper health dashboard with per-airline consecutive error counts, last-scraped timestamps, and live status

title: MyRoomStatus
description: Full-stack hotel property management system (PMS) for the West African market. Runs as a cloud SaaS or a self-contained offline binary — same Go backend, same React frontend, two database drivers.
features: Dual deployment mode: cloud SaaS on PostgreSQL and a standalone offline binary (SQLite, no internet required) built from the same codebase with a single compiler flag
React SPA embedded directly in the Go binary via go:embed — the offline binary is a single executable that serves the entire frontend with no external web server
Offline provisioning via a signed configuration bundle: hotel setup exported from the cloud in one HTTP response and applied to local SQLite via GORM upsert transactions
HMAC-signed periodic sync pushing offline records (bookings, sales, guests, visitors) back to the cloud PostgreSQL instance
Real-time dashboard WebSocket hub broadcasting selective refresh signals scoped per hotel and data section, triggering targeted frontend refetches instead of full reloads
Smart TV push notifications via WebSocket with a pending message queue — messages persisted to DB when a TV is offline and flushed on reconnect
Five smart lock vendors behind a single Provider interface: TTLock, Tuya IoT, Salto KS, ASSA ABLOY Vostio, and DouWin RFID — adding a new vendor only requires implementing the interface

DouWin RFID bridge agent: a separate Go Windows service that loads the vendor DLL, connects to the cloud via a persistent WebSocket, and relays card-issue commands with a SQLite-backed command queue for durability across disconnects
POS/F&B module with inventory tracking, QR-code storefront, partial sales, refunds, and per-category revenue reporting
Flight booking via QuickAir HMAC partner API — hotel staff can search and book flights directly inside the PMS without leaving the platform
Google Gemini AI support chatbot with a hotel-specific markdown knowledge base compiled into the system prompt and driver.js guided tour triggers
Multi-property group reports across hotel chains — occupancy, revenue, P&L, and guest manifests aggregated across all properties in a group
SaaS billing with tiered license plans and optional add-ons (smart TV, F&B, key control, multi-property reports) gated at middleware level
